C2.2.note: Input is a numeric allocation of K votes over candidates, with fractional votes allowed; treated here as cardinal vote allocations.

C2.3.quote: Party leaders and voters share the same objective
C2.3.note: Held attitudes are utilities/objectives over seats won, separately defined from the submitted votes.

C2.4.quote: voters at the polls choose how to cast their votes
C2.4.note: The paper treats held objective over seats and submitted vote allocations as separate objects; voting is chosen strategically.

C3.1.quote: each voter decides whether or not to vote
C3.1.note: All analyses include costly, strategic turnout or vote allocation decisions; the experiment also has participants choose whether to vote.

C3.2.note: C3.1 = ALL, so no non-strategic analyses to code.

C4.1.note: Applicability condition not met: C2.2 is CARD vote allocations, not RANK, WEAK, APPR, DICH, or PAIR.

C4.2.note: The term dichotomous preferences is not used.

C5.1.quote: expected fraction of seats won by the minority is consistently higher
C5.1.note: Minority representation is evaluated through the share of seats won by the minority.

C5.2.quote: expected fraction of seats won by the minority is consistently higher
C5.2.note: Representation is measured from the submitted votes/seat outcomes, not from separately defined utility, and no statement relates this to held attitudes.
